newsitem.title: GERMANY: Hochtief not interested in pooled Holzmann stake.
newsitem.headline: Hochtief not interested in pooled Holzmann stake.

text.p: Construction group Hochtief AG and Deutsche Bank AG, avoiding a battle with Germany's anti-monopoly regulators, said on Monday they were giving up plans to pool their stake in construction firm Philipp Holzmann AG .

The two companies said in a statement they no longer wanted to pursue the scheme after they learned the European Commission would not rule on the plan and would pass the case to the German authorities.
The German Federal Cartel Office had in March rejected the plans of Deutsche Bank and Hochtief and said it wanted to regain responsibility for the Holzmann case from the European Commission.
"Deutsche Bank and Hochtief do not consider it worthwhile to continue with the plan in view of this background," the two companies said in a statement.
Under the original arrangement, Deutsche and Hochtief were to pool stakes totalling almost 50 percent of Holzmann -- Deutsche with 25.8 percent and Hochtief with 20 percent.
The deal would have given Hochtief greater influence in Holzmann's planning, fulfilling a long-standing plan of Hochtief to work more closely with its fellow German builder.
Unable to increase its influence with Holzmann with Deutsche, Hochtief said it would not close the door to buying an additional stake in Holzmann as it had said it would in March.
The builder said it had decided after all against annulling a deal with Commerzbank AG to buy a further 10 percent stake in Holzmann.
In a separate statement, Deutsche Bank said it and Hochtief still wanted to support Holzmann which has racked up losses in the past.
"Both companies remain determined to continue supporting Philipp Holzmann," Deutsche and Hochtief said in a statement.

Hochtief said it wanted to work more closely with Holzmann on overseas projects and said such co-operation was possible in three to six regions and that eventually their foreign operations could be jointly managed.
